heroIntro: Lectures and problem sets for the undergraduate and graduate mathematics courses I teach at IBA Karachi, organised by course and topic so you can find what you need before class, during revision, or the night before an exam.
aboutMe: I am a mathematics educator with a PhD from the Abdus Salam School of Mathematical Sciences, GC University, Lahore. Since 2011, I have taught at the Institute of Business Administration (IBA), Karachi, one of the leading universities in the region. I joined as an Assistant Professor and have been an Associate Professor since 2019. My teaching ranges from first-year Calculus and Linear Algebra, through advanced undergraduate courses in Abstract Algebra, Galois Theory and Topology, to graduate courses in commutative algebra, algebraic curves and category theory.

Alongside my university work, I teach O and A Level Mathematics, Calculus, Linear Algebra, Discrete Mathematics, and other university-level courses. I also prepare students for the IB, SAT, and local board examinations. Many of my students, particularly those I prepared for the SAT, have gone on to study at universities in the United States and Canada.

I always start with the fundamentals, because once you understand why a method works, the problems stop feeling intimidating. From there, we work through practice questions chosen for your level and your weak areas. I also show you how to manage your time and approach exam questions, so that your understanding turns into strong results.
I am patient and welcome every question. My aim is for you to feel supported and confident as you progress at your own pace.

teachingApproach.title: Definitions first, then examples
teachingApproach.text: Each lecture states the key definitions precisely and then works through concrete examples, so the abstract statement and the calculation are seen side by side.

teachingApproach.title: Computation alongside proof
teachingApproach.text: Where it helps, ideas can be checked by computer, for example with the computer algebra system SINGULAR, and course materials are typeset in LaTeX.

teachingApproach.title: Materials you can return to
teachingApproach.text: Lectures stay online for the whole semester, grouped by topic, so revision starts from the same material that was used in class.

research.summary: My research is in computational commutative and non-commutative algebra. I study Sagbi bases and standard bases for subalgebras and modules, their analogues in non-commutative G-algebras, and the classification of singularities, and I implement the resulting algorithms as libraries for the computer algebra system SINGULAR.

software.text: Computes the Sagbi basis of a subalgebra through the Sagbi walk algorithm.

software.name: sagbigrob.lib
software.title: Sagbi-Gröbner Construction Algorithm Library
software.text: Computes the Sagbi basis of an ideal of a subalgebra.

software.name: ncsagbi.lib
software.title: SAGBI Bases in G-Algebras
software.authors: Muhammad Abdul Basit Khan, Junaid Alam Khan
software.text: Implements the SAGBI normal form, the critical-pair criterion and the construction algorithm for SAGBI bases of subalgebras of G-algebras; companion code for Sagbi Bases in G-Algebras (Symmetry, 2019).

software.name: ncsg.lib
software.title: Left Sagbi-Gröbner Bases in G-Algebras
software.authors: Muhammad Abdul Basit Khan, Junaid Alam Khan
software.text: Extends Sagbi-Gröbner bases to G-algebras with left SG-reduction, a Buchberger-style criterion and a terminating algorithm for finite left SG-bases of left ideals in subalgebras.

software.name: nchbasis.lib
software.title: Left H-Bases in Noncommutative G-Algebras
software.authors: Muhammad Abdul Basit Khan, Junaid Alam Khan
software.text: Computes left H-bases of left ideals in G-algebras graded by an integral weight vector (including Weyl algebras and U(sl₂)) using Rees homogenization and an effective syzygy criterion.

software.name: ssbasis.lib
software.title: Subalgebra Standard Bases in Rings with Zero Divisors
software.text: Tests a lifting criterion and completes generating sets to subalgebra standard bases in monoid-graded rings with zero divisors, such as Z/4, Z/6 and dual numbers; includes verification scripts in Python and Lean 4.

bio: Dr. Junaid Alam Khan is Associate Professor of Mathematics in the Department of Mathematical Sciences at the Institute of Business Administration (IBA), Karachi, where he has taught since 2011.

He received his Ph.D. in Mathematics from the Abdus Salam School of Mathematical Sciences, GC University, Lahore, in 2011, under the supervision of Prof. Dr. Gerhard Pfister. He earned his M.Sc. in Pure Mathematics from the University of Karachi with a First Class, Third Position, after a B.Sc. in Mathematics at the same university.

He chaired the Department of Mathematical Sciences at IBA from 2016 to 2019 and directed IBA's Talent Hunt Programs from 2019 to 2025. He received the HEC Best University Teacher Award in 2018 and the IBA Best Teacher Award in 2017.
